claims.summary: Proposed Exception Growth Audit: diff core.rs against a stable snapshot and trigger manual review when the delta exceeds a complexity threshold (e.g. 10% increase in unique function signatures), protecting the zero-growth ratchet principle.
claims.disposition: Implemented this round, at her exact threshold. scripts/domain_boundary_audit.py now counts unique fn signatures per documented cohesion exception and fails verify with the new exception_signature_growth violation kind when the count exceeds the file's maximum_unique_fn_signatures ceiling in domain_boundaries_v1.toml. Ceilings seeded for all seven exception files at current count plus 10% headroom (core.rs 210 -> 232, orchestration 6 -> 7, bridge_state 24 -> 27, structure 11 -> 13, encoding 9 -> 10, fallback_weights 1 -> 2, transport 37 -> 41). The counter audit gains documented_exception_signature_ceilings_hold, and a focused regression proves a signature increase trips the audit even when the line count stays within its line ceiling. DOMAIN_BOUNDARIES.md documents the new ratchet. This is read-only steward/CI evidence tooling; it grants no runtime authority and changes no live behavior.
